body.text: atha śrīvātūlanāthasūtrāṇi

children.translated_text: Together with the commentary composed by the glorious <s>Anantaśaktipāda</s>

body.translated_text: Now, the Sūtras of the Glorious <s>Vātūlanātha</s>

children.translated_text: That which shines forth everywhere with the <s>khecarī</s> (sky-moving) vision — the changeless state arisen from the force of the union of the clash, the realm beyond the void of the void, whose essence is imperishable awakening —

children.text: sarvatra khecaradṛśā pravirājate yat tan naumi sāhasavaraṃ guruvaktragamyam
children.translated_text: I bow to that supreme act of daring, accessible through the mouth of the <s>guru</s>.

children.text: sarvatra khecara-dṛśā pravirājate yat tan naumi sāhasa-varaṃ guru-vaktra-gamyam

children.translated_text: Transcending all activities here, without fixed abode, beyond sequence and non-sequence,
some indescribable sky of supreme consciousness, self-natured — may the unborn be victorious!
That which has arisen from the ocean-heart of the glorious <s>Vātūlanātha</s>,
which has cast off worship, worshipper, and acts of worship — I bow to that.
By which, here, though always situated in the midst of all activities,
I abide, having entered the great sky, without succession, in this —
clashing of the intention of the conceptualization of consciousness — I bow to the unsurpassed.
The supreme commentary on the sūtras born from the mouth of the <s>yoginīs</s>
is composed correctly by someone, nourished by the supreme reality.

body.text:
iha kila ṣaḍdarśanacaturāmnāyādimelāpaparyantasamastadarśanottīrṇam akathyam api śrīmadvātūlanāthasya pīṭheśvaryocchuṣmapādaugham uktvā tad anu paramarahasyopabṛṃhitatrayodaśakathāsākātkāradṛśā kramākramāstināstitathyātathyabhedābhedasavikalpanirvikalpabhavanirvāṇakalaṅkojjhitaṃ kim apy anavakāśaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ sūtramukhenādiśanti -
yatredam ādisūtram
body.translated_text: Here indeed, transcending all doctrines including the six philosophical systems and the four <s>āmnāyas</s> (sacred traditions) up to their union — though inexpressible — having stated the lineage of <s>Ucchuṣma</s> and the lord of the <s>pīṭha</s> of the glorious <s>Vātūlanātha</s>, then after that, with a vision that directly realizes the thirteen discourses nourished by the supreme secret, free from the stain of sequence and non-sequence, existence and non-existence, truth and untruth, difference and non-difference, conceptual and non-conceptual, worldly existence and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — they teach through the medium of sūtras some supreme reality that is without scope and beyond all — wherein this is the first sūtra:

children.text:
iha kila ṣaḍ-darśana-catur-āmnāya-ādi-melāpa-paryanta-samasta-darśana-uttīrṇam akathyam api śrīmad-vātūlanāthasya pīṭheśvarya ucchuṣma-pāda-augham uktvā tad anu parama-rahasya-upabṛṃhita-trayodaśa-kathā-sākātkāra-dṛśā krama-akrama-asti-nāsti-tathya-atathya-bheda-abheda-savikalpa-nirvikalpa-bhava-nirvāṇa-kalaṅka-ujjhitaṃ kim apy anavakāśaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ sūtra-mukhenā adiśanti --
yatra idam ādi-sūtram

body.text: mahāsāhasavṛttyā svarūpalābhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Through the activity of the great daring, the attainment of one's own true nature.

body.text: atitīvrātitīvrataraviśṛṅkhalaśaktipātāghrātasya svasvarūpasamāviṣṭasya kasya cit kva cit kadā cid akasmād eva "*mahāsāhasavṛttyā*" ghasmaramahāghanataraparanādollāsasphāreṇa savikalpanirvikalpātmakasamastasaṃvinnivahaghaṭṭanān nirāvaraṇamahāśūnyatāsamāveśaniṣṭhayā "*svarūpalābhaḥ*" samastakalpanottīrṇatvād akṛtakaniravakāśaniruttaranistaraṅganiravadhinirniketāsparśasaṃvitprāptir bhavati - iti rahasyārthaḥ / mahāsāhasavṛttyānupraveśaś ca vakṣyamāṇakathitakrameṇādhigantavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For someone, somewhere, at some time, who has been touched by the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) that is exceedingly intense, even more intense, and utterly unrestrained, who has entered into one's own true nature — suddenly, through the "activity of the great daring," by the expansion of the resounding of the supreme <s>nāda</s> (vibration) that is intensely dense and all-consuming, through the clashing of the entire aggregate of awareness consisting of both the conceptual and the non-conceptual, by the culmination of the entry into the great void without any covering — "the attainment of one's own true nature" occurs: the attainment of the awareness that transcends all mental construction, that is uncreated, without scope, without answer, without waves, without limit, without abode, and untouched — this is the secret meaning. And the entry through the activity of the great daring is to be understood through the method of discourse that will be explained.

children.text: ati-tīvrātitīvratara-viśṛṅkhala-śaktipāta-āghrātasya sva-svarūpa-samāviṣṭasya kasya cit kva cit kadā cid akasmād eva "*mahā-sāhasavṛttyā*" ghasmara-mahāghanatara-para-nāda-ullāsa-sphāreṇa savikalpa-nirvikalpa-ātmaka-samasta-saṃvin-nivaha-ghaṭṭanān nirāvaraṇa-mahāśūnyatā-samāveśa-niṣṭhayā "*svarūpa-lābhaḥ*" samasta-kalpanā-uttīrṇatvād akṛtaka-niravakāśa-niruttara-nistaraṅga-niravadhi-nirniketa-asparśa-saṃvit-prāptir bhavati -- iti rahasya-arthaḥ / mahāsāhasa-vṛttya ānupraveśaś ca vakṣyamāṇa-kathita-krameṇa adhigantavyaḥ //

body.text: jhaṭiti sarvollaṅghanakrameṇāniketasvarūpaprāptisākṣātkāramahāsāhasacarcāsaṃpradāyaṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ tatraiva sarvavṛttimahāsāmarasyam ekakāle pracakṣate
body.translated_text: Having established the tradition of the discourse on the great daring — the direct realization of the attainment of the abode-less true nature through the method of sudden transcendence of all — now they declare the great equality of all activities in that very state, simultaneously:

children.text: jhaṭiti sarva-ullaṅghana-krameṇa aniketa-svarūpa-prāpti-sākṣātkāra-mahā-sāhasa-carcā-saṃpradāyaṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ tatraiva sarva-vṛtti-mahā-sāmarasyam ekakāle pracakṣate

body.text: tallābhācchuritā [yud?]yugapadvṛttipravṛttiḥ
body.translated_text: From the attainment of that, the simultaneous arising of all activities, imbued [by it].

body.text: vṛttīnāṃ dṛgādimarīcirūpāṇāṃ tathā rāgadveṣādyunmeṣavatīnāṃ "*yugapat*" tulyakālaṃ kramaparipāṭyullaṅghanenākramapravṛttyā "*tallābhācchuritā*" tat tena prāguktamahāsāhasadaśāsamāveśakramaprāpyeṇa svarūpalābhena kālākālakalpanottīrṇālaṃgrāsavapuṣā mahānirīheṇācchuritā spṛṣtā svasvarūpatāṃ nītāḷ"*pravṛttir*" prakarṣeṇa vartamānā vṛttir satatam acyutatayā tatsamāveśāvasthānam ity arthaḥ / ity anayoktibhaṅgyā sarvavṛttīnāṃ samanantaram eva sarvottīrṇamahāśūnyatādhāmni dhāmarūpe tanmayatayā parasparavibhedavigalanenodayapadavyām eva satatam avasthitir sthitetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Of the activities — which have the form of rays such as sight and so forth, and which are attended by the arising of desire, aversion, and the like — "simultaneously," meaning at the same time, by transcending sequential order through non-sequential arising, "imbued by the attainment of that" — that is, touched and brought to their own true nature by the attainment of one's own true nature, which is to be obtained through the method of entry into the state of the great daring described earlier, whose body is the great devouring that transcends the conceptualization of time and non-time, by the great effortlessness — "arising" means activity that is occurring with intensity, as a constant unfallen abiding in that state of absorption. Thus by this manner of expression, the meaning is that immediately upon the arising of all activities, there is constant abiding in the very state of emergence, through their becoming one with the supreme abode of the great void that transcends everything, which has the form of the abode, through the dissolution of mutual distinction.

children.text: vṛttīnāṃ dṛg-ādi-marīci-rūpāṇāṃ tathā rāga-dveṣa-ādy-unmeṣavatīnāṃ "*yugapat*" tulyakālaṃ krama-paripāṭy-ullaṅghanena akrama-pravṛttyā "*tal-lābha-ācchuritā*" tat tena prāg-ukta-mahāsāhasa-daśā-samāveśa-krama-prāpyeṇa svarūpa-lābhena kāla-akāla-kalpanā-uttīrṇa-alaṃgrāsa-vapuṣā mahānirīheṇā acchuritā spṛṣtā sva-svarūpatāṃ nītāḷ"*pravṛttir-*" prakarṣeṇa vartamānā vṛttir satatam acyutatayā tat-samāveśa-avasthānam ity arthaḥ / ity anaya ūkti-bhaṅgyā sarva-vṛttīnāṃ samanantaram eva sarva-uttīrṇa-mahā-śūnyatā-dhāmni dhāma-rūpe tanmayatayā paraspara-vibheda-vigalanena udaya-padavyām eva satatam avasthitir sthita īty-arthaḥ //

body.text: ityanayoktibhaṅgyā tulyakālakathanopadeśam uktvedānīṃ pustakakathāṃ nirūpayanti
body.translated_text: Having thus spoken the teaching of simultaneous discourse in this manner of expression, they now expound the book-discourse:

children.text: ity-anaya ūkti-bhaṅgyā tulya-kāla-kathana-upadeśam uktva īdānīṃ pustaka-kathāṃ nirūpayanti

body.text: ubhayapaṭṭodghaṭṭanān mahāśūnyatāpraveśaḥ
body.translated_text: Through the opening of both sides, entry into the great void.

body.text:
śrīmanniṣkriyānandanāthānugrahasamaye śrīgandhamādanasiddhapādair akṛtakapustakapradarśanena yā parapade prāptir upadiṣṭā saiva vitatya nirūpyate / saptarandhrakramoditasaptaśikhollāsātmakaḥ prāṇapravāhodayaḥ saivordhvapaṭṭakaḥ pūrṇavṛttyudayaḥ, randhradvayasuṣiranālikāpravāhaprasṛto 'pānarūpo 'dhaḥpaṭṭakaḥ pañcendriyaśaktiveṣṭitaḥ pañcaphaṇadharmānibandhako 'dhaḥsthitaḥ / tasya valayadvayaṃ jāgratsvapnātmakam unmudrya granthinibandhanam apahṛtya "*ubhayapaṭṭodghaṭṭanāt*" prāṇāpānadvayavidāraṇān madhyavartī yaḥ prāṇarūpo mahāśūnyatāsvabhāvaḥ kulākulavikalpadaśojjhito 'vyapadeśyamahānirāvaraṇaniratyayavedyavedakanirmukto varṇāvarṇanivarṇottīrṇaḥ sparśāsparśaprathāparivarjitopacārāt paramākāśādyabhidhānaiḥ
abhidhīyate / tatra "*praveśaḥ*" tatsamāveśatayā sāmarasyāvasthitir saiva prāptamahopadeśanāmāvirbhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: At the time of the grace of the illustrious <s>Niṣkriyānanda Nātha</s>, the very same attainment of the supreme state (<s>parapada</s>) that was taught by the illustrious <s>Gandhamādana Siddhapāda</s> through the showing of the uncreated book is now elaborated in detail. The arising of the <s>prāṇa</s>-flow, consisting of the blossoming of seven crests (<s>saptaśikhā</s>) arisen through the sequence of seven apertures (<s>saptarandhra</s>), is itself the upper current (<s>ūrdhvapaṭṭaka</s>), the arising of full activity (<s>pūrṇavṛtti</s>). The <s>apāna</s>-form flowing through the hollow channel of the two apertures, enveloped by the powers of the five senses, bound by the five-hooded principles, stationed below — that is the lower current (<s>adhaḥpaṭṭaka</s>). Having unsealed its two coils (<s>valaya</s>) — consisting of waking and dream — and removed the knot-binding (<s>granthinibandha</s>), 'from the striking open of both currents' (<s>ubhayapaṭṭodghaṭṭana</s>), by the splitting of the pair of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, the middle-dwelling [principle] which is of the nature of <s>prāṇa</s>, whose essential nature is great voidness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), free from the condition of <s>kula</s>-<s>akula</s> conceptual distinction, inexpressible, great, without covering, without limit, free from known and knower, transcending colored and colorless, and free from the manifestation of touch and non-touch — is figuratively spoken of by designations such as 'supreme space' (<s>paramākāśa</s>) and the like. There, 'entry' (<s>praveśa</s>) means staying in equilibrium (<s>sāmarasya</s>) through absorption into that; that itself manifests as the attained 'great teaching' (<s>mahopadeśa</s>) — this is the meaning.

children.text:
śrīman-niṣkriyānandanātha-anugraha-samaye śrīgandhamādana-siddha-pādair akṛtaka-pustaka-pradarśanena yā para-pade prāptir upadiṣṭā sa aiva vitatya nirūpyate / sapta-randhra-krama-udita-sapta-śikhā-ullāsa-ātmakaḥ prāṇa-pravāha-udayaḥ sa evā urdhva-paṭṭakaḥ pūrṇa-vṛtty-udayaḥ, randhra-dvaya-suṣira-nālikā-pravāha-prasṛto 'pāna-rūpo 'dhaḥ-paṭṭakaḥ pañca-indriya-śakti-veṣṭitaḥ pañca-phaṇa-dharma-anibandhako 'dhaḥsthitaḥ / tasya valaya-dvayaṃ jāgrat-svapna-ātmakam unmudrya granthi-nibandhanam apahṛtya "*ubhaya-paṭṭa-udghaṭṭanāt*" prāṇa-apāna-dvaya-vidāraṇān madhya-vartī yaḥ prāṇa-rūpo mahā-śūnyatā-svabhāvaḥ kula-akula-vikalpa-daśā-ujjhito 'vyapadeśya-mahā-nirāvaraṇaniratyaya-vedya-vedaka-nirmukto varṇa-avarṇa-nivarṇa-uttīrṇaḥ sparśa-asparśa-prathā-parivarjita upacārāt parama-ākāśa-ādy-abhidhānaiḥ
abhidhīyate / tatra "*praveśaḥ*" tat-samāveśatayā sāmarasya-avasthitir sa eva prāpta-mahā-upadeśa-nāmā avirbhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: itthaṃ mahānayoktadṛśā sarvaśāstraprapañcottīrṇātvād avācyaṃ kim api mahopadeśasākṣātkāram ubhayapaṭṭakākārasadasadrūpadvayanivāraṇena nistaraṅgaparavyomasamāveśavivarjitam āsūtritamahāśūnyatāsamāveśam āvedya, idānīṃ yugmopasaṃhārāt kaivalyaphalaṃ tanmayatopavarṇyate
body.translated_text: Thus, because from the perspective of the great doctrine (<s>mahānaya</s>), it transcends the elaboration of all scriptures, having communicated the ineffable direct realization of the great teaching — the absorption into great voidness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>) that is threaded through, free from the immersion into the waveless supreme sky (<s>nistaraṅgaparavyoma</s>) — through the removal of both forms of existent and non-existent appearing as the two currents (<s>paṭṭaka</s>), now the fruit of isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) from the absorption of the pair is described as immersion in that:

children.text: itthaṃ mahānaya-uktadṛśā sarvaśāstra-prapañca-uttīrṇātvād avācyaṃ kim api mahā-upadeśa-sākṣātkāram ubhaya-paṭṭaka-ākāra-sad-asad-rūpa-dvaya-nivāraṇena nistaraṅga-paravyoma-samāveśa-vivarjitam āsūtrita-mahāśūnyatā-samāveśam āvedya, idānīṃ yugma-upasaṃhārāt kaivalyaphalaṃ tanmayata ūpavarṇyate

body.text: yugmagrāsān niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā //
body.translated_text: From the devouring of the pair (<s>yugmagrāsa</s>), [there arises] the establishment in awareness without gap (<s>niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā</s>).

body.text:
pṛthivyādimahābhūtapañcakasyaikaikasmin grāhyagrāhakatayā "*yugma*" vṛttyudayasaṃvyavasthitiḥ / tatra gandhaprādhānyād dharātattvasya pāyughrāṇarūpeṇa dviprakāratā / aptattvasya ca rasapradhānatayopastharasanārūpeṇadvaividhyam / tejastattvasya rūpaprādhānyāt pādanetrabhedena dvayarūpatā / vāyutattvasya sparśaprādhānyāt tvakpāṇisvabhāvato dvidhā gatiḥ / ākāśatattvasya śabdaprādhānyād vākśrotrabhedena dviprakāratayaiva bahudhātvam / athavā pṛthivyapsvarūpau bhogyasvarūpāvasthitau / tejovāyvākhyau bhoktṛsvabhāvau saṃsthitau / ākāśaṃ caitad yugmāntarasthaṃ satsuṣiratayā sarvapranāḍikāntaroditaṃ ca bahudhā vibhaktam / pṛthivyādivāyvantaṃ bhūtacatuṣṭayaṃ bhogyarūpam ākāśaṃ ca bhoktṛsvabhāvam iti vā / bhogye 'pi bhoktā sadaiva tiṣṭhati; bhoktary api bhogaḥ
nityaṃ vibhāti / evamuktayuktyā pratyekaṃ pṛthivyādimahābhūtapañcakaṃ yugmena dvayavibhūtyānārataṃ prollasatītyabhiprāyaḥ / athavā pratyekaṃ vyaktāvyaktatayā bahirantaratayā śāntodriktatayā vā vibhāti / etat pañcakasthānasaṃthitayugmasya ``grāsāt'' saṃharaṇat ``niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā'' niravakāśā yeyaṃ saṃvit tasyā niṣṭhā samyagaviparyastatayā saṃthitiḥ / niravakāśasaṃvittvena nāpi savikalpasaṃvidunmeṣair avakāśo labhyate, nāpi nirvikalpasaṃvitsvabhāvena praveśo 'dhigamyate / ittham aprameyatvān niruttaraparamādvayasvabhāvatvāc ca niravakāśasaṃvid ihocyate / tasyā niṣṭhā varagurupradarśitadṛśā satatam ucyatā gatir keṣāṃcid bhavatīty arthaḥ / evaṃ dvayātmakakulakaulakavalanena nirupādhinīrūpaniḥsvarūpatādātmyaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ //4//
body.translated_text: For each of the five great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) beginning with earth, a 'pair' (<s>yugma</s>) is the establishment of dual appearance as grasped and grasper (<s>grāhyagrāhaka</s>). There: the earth principle (<s>dharātattva</s>), with smell as predominant, has two forms as the organ of excretion (<s>pāyu</s>) and nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>). The water principle (<s>aptattva</s>), with taste as predominant, has duality as the organ of generation (<s>upastha</s>) and tongue (<s>rasanā</s>). The fire principle (<s>tejastattva</s>), with form as predominant, has two forms as feet (<s>pāda</s>) and eyes (<s>netra</s>). The air principle (<s>vāyutattva</s>), with touch as predominant, has a dual course as skin (<s>tvak</s>) and hands (<s>pāṇi</s>). The space principle (<s>ākāśatattva</s>), with sound as predominant, has multiplicity through duality as speech (<s>vāk</s>) and hearing (<s>śrotra</s>). Or alternatively: earth and water are established as objects of enjoyment (<s>bhogya</s>); fire and air are established as the nature of the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>); and space, standing between these pairs, is divided in many ways as it pervades all channels in the form of the hollow (<s>suṣira</s>). Or: the four elements from earth to air are the form of the enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>), and space is the nature of the enjoyer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>). The enjoyer always abides in the enjoyed; enjoyment always shines in the enjoyer. Thus by this reasoning, each of the five great elements constantly shines forth through the dual manifestation of the pair — this is the intended meaning. Or: each shines as manifest and unmanifest, as outer and inner, or as quiescent and arisen. 'From the devouring (<s>grāsa</s>)' — from the absorption — of the pair stationed in these five stations, [there arises] 'the establishment in awareness without gap (<s>niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā</s>)' — the settling of that awareness which is without gap, properly and without distortion. By being awareness without gap, neither is there occasion found for the opening of conceptual awareness (<s>savikalpasaṃvid</s>), nor is entry into the nature of non-conceptual awareness (<s>nirvikalpasaṃvid</s>) attained. Thus, because it is immeasurable and because its nature is the supreme non-dual without superior (<s>niruttaraparamādvaya</s>), this awareness without gap is spoken of here. Its establishment, through the vision shown by the excellent <s>guru</s>, is said to be the constantly spoken attainment of some — this is the meaning. Thus, by the devouring of the pair-natured <s>kula</s> and <s>kaulika</s>, there arises identity with the unconditioned formlessness that is free from essential nature — this is the meaning. // 4 //

children.text:
pṛthivy-ādi-mahābhūta-pañcakasya eka-ekasmin grāhya-grāhakatayā "*yugma*" -vṛtty-udaya-saṃvyavasthitiḥ / tatra gandha-prādhānyād dharā-tattvasya pāyu-ghrāṇa-rūpeṇa dvi-prakāratā / ap-tattvasya ca rasa-pradhānataya ūpastha-rasanā-rūpeṇadvaividhyam / tejas-tattvasya rūpaprādhānyāt pāda-netra-bhedena dvaya-rūpatā / vāyu-tattvasya sparśa-prādhānyāt tvak-pāṇi-svabhāvato dvidhā gatiḥ / ākāśa-tattvasya śabda-prādhānyād vāk-śrotra-bhedena dvi-prakārataya aiva bahudhātvam / athavā pṛthivy-ap-svarūpau bhogya-svarūpa-avasthitau / tejo-vāyv-ākhyau bhoktṛ-svabhāvau saṃsthitau / ākāśaṃ ca etad yugma-antarasthaṃ sat-suṣiratayā sarva-pranāḍikā-antara-uditaṃ ca bahudhā vibhaktam / pṛthivy-ādi-vāyv-antaṃ bhūta-catuṣṭayaṃ bhogya-rūpam ākāśaṃ ca bhoktṛ-svabhāvam iti vā / bhogye 'pi bhoktā sada aiva tiṣṭhati; bhoktary api bhogaḥ
nityaṃ vibhāti / evam-ukta-yuktyā pratyekaṃ pṛthivy-ādi-mahā-bhūta-pañcakaṃ yugmena dvaya-vibhūtya ānārataṃ prollasati ity-abhiprāyaḥ / athavā pratyekaṃ vyakta-avyaktatayā bahir-antaratayā śānta-udriktatayā vā vibhāti / etat pañcaka-sthāna-saṃthita-yugmasya ``grāsāt'' saṃharaṇat- ``niravakāśa-saṃvin-niṣṭhā'' niravakāśā ya īyaṃ saṃvit tasyā niṣṭhā samyag-aviparyastatayā saṃthitiḥ / niravakāśa-saṃvittvena na api savikalpa-saṃvid-unmeṣair avakāśo labhyate, na api nirvikalpa-saṃvit-svabhāvena praveśo 'dhigamyate / ittham aprameyatvān niruttara-paramādvaya-svabhāvatvāc ca niravakāśa-saṃvid iha ucyate / tasyā niṣṭhā vara-guru-pradarśita-dṛśā satatam ucyatā gatir keṣāṃcid bhavati ity arthaḥ / evaṃ dvayā atmaka-kula-kaula-kavalanena nirupādhi-nīrūpa-niḥsvarūpa-tādātmyaṃ bhavati ity arthaḥ //4//

body.text: dvayavigalanena paratattvāvasthitiṃ yugmacarcāgamanikayehoktvā, tad anu saṃghaṭṭakathāsākṣātkāro nirūpyate
body.translated_text: Having spoken through the tradition (<s>nikāya</s>) of pair-discourse (<s>yugmacarcā</s>) about the establishment in the supreme reality (<s>paratattva</s>) through the dissolution of duality (<s>dvayavigalana</s>), next the direct realization of the encounter-narrative (<s>saṃghaṭṭakathā</s>) is elaborated:

children.text: dvaya-vigalanena para-tattva-avasthitiṃ yugma-carcāgamanikaya īha uktvā, tad anu saṃghaṭṭa-kathā-sākṣātkāro nirūpyate

body.text: siddhayoginīsaṃghaṭṭān mahāmelāpodayaḥ
body.translated_text: From the encounter (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) of <s>siddhas</s> and <s>yoginīs</s>, [there arises] the emergence of the great assembly (<s>mahāmelāpa</s>).

body.text: siddhā ca yoginyaś ca tā siddhayoginyo viṣayakaraṇeśvarīrūpā / tāsāṃ saṃghaṭṭaḥ saṃgamo grāhyagrāhakobhayasaṃśleṣaḥ parasparāgūraṇakrameṇāliṅganam / tenāliṅganena sadaiva ``mahāmelāpodayaḥ'' mahāmelāpasyāhaṃtedaṃtātmakadvayavigalanān niruttaracidvyomni satataṃ mahāsāmarasyātmakasya sarvatra pratyakṣatayodayaḥ samullāso bhavatīty arthaḥ / vedyavedakadvayāprathanapravṛttyā paramādvayasamāveśaḥ sarvatrāvasthitety uktaṃ bhavati //5//
body.translated_text: The <s>siddhas</s> (accomplished ones) and <s>yoginīs</s> — they are the <s>siddhayoginīs</s>, having the form of sovereign mistresses of objects and sense-organs. Their meeting (<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s>) is the conjunction, the fusion of both the apprehended and the apprehender (<s>grāhyagrāhaka</s>), an embrace through the process of mutual interpenetration. By that embrace, always, 'the arising of the great meeting (<s>mahāmelāpa</s>)' — the meaning is: through the dissolution of the duality consisting of 'I-ness' (<s>ahaṃtā</s>) and 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃtā</s>), the joyful emergence — as direct perception everywhere, constantly in the unsurpassed sky of consciousness (<s>cidvyoman</s>) — of that which has the nature of supreme equality (<s>mahāsāmarasya</s>) occurs. Through the activity of the non-manifestation of the duality of the known and the knower, the immersion in the supreme non-duality (<s>paramādvayasamāveśa</s>) is established everywhere — this is what is stated. // 5 //

children.text: siddhā ca yoginyaś ca tā siddhayoginyo viṣaya-karaṇeśvarī-rūpā / tāsāṃ saṃghaṭṭaḥ saṃgamo grāhya-grāhaka-ubhaya-saṃśleṣaḥ paraspara-āgūraṇa-krameṇā aliṅganam / tenā aliṅganena sada aiva ``mahāmelāpa-udayaḥ'' mahāmelāpasya ahaṃtā-idaṃtā-ātmaka-dvaya-vigalanān niruttara-cidvyomni satataṃ mahāsāmarasya-ātmakasya sarvatra pratyakṣataya ūdayaḥ samullāso bhavati ity arthaḥ / vedya-vedaka-dvaya-aprathana-pravṛttyā paramādvaya-samāveśaḥ sarvatra avasthita ity uktaṃ bhavati //5//

body.text: ubhayavigalanena sadaiva mahāmelāpodayam uktvā, tad anu kañcukatrayollaṅghanena niruttarapadaprāptiṃ kaṭākṣayanti
body.translated_text: Having stated the arising of the great meeting through the dissolution of both [subject and object] always, next they hint at the attainment of the unsurpassed state (<s>niruttarapada</s>) through the transcendence of the three sheaths (<s>kañcukatraya</s>):

children.text: ubhaya-vigalanena sada aiva mahāmelāpa-udayam uktvā, tad anu kañcuka-traya-ullaṅghanena niruttara-pada-prāptiṃ kaṭākṣayanti

body.text: trikañcukaparityāgān nirākhyapadāvasthitiḥ
body.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 6:] Through the abandonment of the three sheaths (<s>trikañcuka</s>), [there is] establishment in the nameless state (<s>nirākhyapada</s>).

body.text: trikañcukasya bhāvikabhautikaśūnyabhedabhinnasya / tatra bhāvikaṃ śabdādyahaṃkāraparyantaṃ tanmātrarūpaṃ, bhautikaṃ pṛthivyādirūpaṃ, śūnyaṃ nirīhākhyaṃ vāsanāsvarūpaṃ ca / athavā bhāvikaṃ ghaṭākāraṃ bāhyaṃ grāhyaviṣayarūpaṃ, bhautikaṃ puno'antaram indriyātmakaṃ grahaṇarūpam, śūnyaṃ tadubhayamadhyamākāśam / athavā bhāvikaṃ svapnāvasthā sṛṣṭir ucyate, bhautikaṃ jāgratprathā sthitir nigadyate, śūnyaṃ suṣuptadaśā saṃhāro 'bhidhīyate / itthaṃsaṃsthitasya trikañcukasya ``parityāgāt'' sannyāsāt ``nirākhyapadāvasthitir''nirgatākhyābhidhānaṃ yasyāsau nirākhyo 'vyapadeśyam anuttaraṃ vāguttīrṇaṃ paraṃ dhāma, tasmin sarvottīrṇāniketanaparamākāśe 'vasthitir sadaivāparicyutasvabhāvaniṣṭhā bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ //6//
body.translated_text: The three sheaths are divided into the categories of the subtle (<s>bhāvika</s>), the material (<s>bhautika</s>), and the void (<s>śūnya</s>). Among these, the subtle extends from sound etc. up to ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), in the form of the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>); the material is in the form of earth etc.; and the void, known as 'without impulse' (<s>nirīhā</s>), has the nature of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). Alternatively, the subtle is external, in the form of an apprehended object such as a pot; the material is internal, consisting of the sense-organs, in the form of apprehension; and the void is the space between those two. Or again, the subtle is the dream state, called 'creation' (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>); the material is the waking state, called 'maintenance' (<s>sthiti</s>); and the void is the state of deep sleep, called 'dissolution' (<s>saṃhāra</s>). Through the 'abandonment,' the renunciation, of the three sheaths so constituted, [there is] 'establishment in the nameless state' (<s>nirākhyapada</s>) — [that state] whose name has departed, i.e., the undesignatable, unsurpassed, transcending speech, the supreme abode — in that all-transcending, shelterless, supreme sky, the establishment is a constant abiding whose nature never departs from its own essence — this is the connection. // 6 //

children.text: trikañcukasya bhāvika-bhautika-śūnya-bheda-bhinnasya / tatra bhāvikaṃ śabda-ādy-ahaṃkāra-paryantaṃ tanmātra-rūpaṃ, bhautikaṃ pṛthivy-ādi-rūpaṃ, śūnyaṃ nirīha-ākhyaṃ vāsanā-svarūpaṃ ca / athavā bhāvikaṃ ghaṭa-ākāraṃ bāhyaṃ grāhya-viṣaya-rūpaṃ, bhautikaṃ puno-'antaram indriya-ātmakaṃ grahaṇa-rūpam, śūnyaṃ tad-ubhaya-madhyama-ākāśam / athavā bhāvikaṃ svapna-avasthā sṛṣṭir ucyate, bhautikaṃ jāgrat-prathā sthitir nigadyate, śūnyaṃ suṣupta-daśā saṃhāro 'bhidhīyate / itthaṃ-saṃsthitasya trikañcukasya ``parityāgāt'' sannyāsāt ``nirākhya-pada-avasthitir-''nirgatā ākhya ābhidhānaṃ yasya asau nirākhyo 'vyapadeśyam anuttaraṃ vāg-uttīrṇaṃ paraṃ dhāma, tasmin sarvottīrṇa-aniketana-paramākāśe 'vasthitir sada aiva aparicyuta-svabhāva-niṣṭhā bhavati iti saṃbandhaḥ //6//

body.text: itthaṃ kañcukatrayollaṅghanena turyapadaprāptiṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ sarvavākprathāsu nirāvaraṇāsu svarabhūtivijṛmbhaiva prathate sadaiva, - iti nirūpayanti
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the attainment of the fourth state (<s>turya</s>) through the transcendence of the three sheaths, now [the text] demonstrates that in all the expansions of speech, which are without covering, it is the unfurling of the resonance-power (<s>svarabhūtivijṛmbha</s>) alone that manifests perpetually:

children.text: itthaṃ kañcuka-traya-ullaṅghanena turya-pada-prāptiṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ sarva-vāk-prathāsu nirāvaraṇāsu svara-bhūti-vijṛmbha aiva prathate sada aiva, -- iti nirūpayanti

body.text: vākcatuṣṭayodayavirāmaprathāsu svaraḥ prathate
body.translated_text: [<s>Sūtra</s> 7:] In the manifestations of the arising and cessation of the fourfold speech (<s>vākcatuṣṭaya</s>), the resonance (<s>svara</s>) manifests.

body.text:
ādau tāvad vākcatuṣṭayaṃ nirṇīyate / nirāvaraṇaniravakāśodayaniruttaranistaraṅgaparamanabhasy ucchalatkimciccalanātmakaprathamaspandavikāsasvabhāvā varṇaracanāṃ māyūrāṇḍarasanyāyenādvayamahāsāmarasyatayāntodhārayantī pareti prathitā / saiva cānāhatanādasvarūpatām avāptā nirvibhāgadharmiṇī samastavarṇodayaṃ vaṭadhānikāvad antodhārayantī draṣṭṛsvabhāvā paśyantīti vyapadeśyā / saiva ca saṃkalpavikalpanivahaniścayātmabuddhibhūmiṃ svīkṛtavatī varṇapuñjaṃ śimbikāphalanyāyenāntodhārayantī madhyametyabhihitā / saiva hṛtkaṇṭhatālvādisthānakaraṇakrameṇāhatā satī varṇavibhavamayaślokādivad bhedarūpaṃ prakaṭayantī rūpādisamastaviśvaprathāṃ ca vyaktatām āpādayantī vaikharīty uktā / itthaṃ niravakāśāt saṃvitpadāt
vākcatuṣṭayam aviratam anirodhatayā prathate / evam īdṛksvabhāvavākcatuṣṭayasyodayaś ca virāmaś ca tāvad udayavirāmau sṛṣṭisaṃhārau, tayor prathā vyaktāvyaktatayā sadaivāviratam ullasantyaḥ sphurantyaḥ, tāsu ``svaraḥ'' anāhatahatottīrṇamahānādollāsavikāsasvabhāvaḥ ``prathate'' savikalpanirvikalpasaṃviduttīrṇaparaviyadudayam eva prakāśitaṃ satatam akaraṇapravṛttyā prayātīty arthaḥ / itthaṃ nānābhedollāsaprakāśarūpeṣu varṇanivahodvahodayeṣu madhyāt prativarṇāntare vākcatuṣṭayakrameṇākhaṇḍitavṛttyā svasvarūpam aparityajya yathāmukhopadiṣṭanītyā svaraiva prathate, -- ityuktaṃ bhavati //7//
body.translated_text: First, the fourfold speech is determined. In the supreme sky that is uncovered, spaceless in its arising, unsurpassed, and waveless — having the nature of the first throb's (<s>spanda</s>) unfurling, which is a slight stirring emerging [in consciousness] — sustaining the arrangement of phonemes within herself by the logic of the peacock-egg fluid [where all colors exist undifferentiated], through non-dual supreme equality (<s>advayamahāsāmarasya</s>) — she is known as <s>parā</s> (the supreme [speech]). She herself, having attained the nature of the unstruck sound (<s>anāhatanāda</s>), possessing the quality of non-differentiation, sustaining the arising of all phonemes within herself like a banyan seed (<s>vaṭadhānikā</s>), having the nature of the seer — is designated as <s>paśyantī</s> (the seeing [speech]). She herself, having adopted the ground of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) whose nature is determination from a mass of intentions and conceptualizations (<s>saṃkalpavikalpa</s>), sustaining the aggregate of phonemes within herself by the logic of the silk-cotton fruit (<s>śimbikāphala</s>) — is called <s>madhyamā</s> (the middle [speech]). She herself, being struck through the process of articulatory positions and instruments such as the heart, throat, palate, etc., manifesting differentiated form like verses and the like, rich in phonemic splendor, and bringing to manifest expression the entire universal expansion of form and other [sense objects] — is called <s>vaikharī</s> (the manifest [speech]). Thus, from the spaceless ground of consciousness (<s>saṃvitpada</s>), the fourfold speech manifests unceasingly, without obstruction. Now, the arising and cessation of this fourfold speech having such a nature — the arising and cessation being creation and dissolution — their manifestation constantly flashing forth in both manifest and unmanifest ways; in them, the 'resonance' (<s>svara</s>), whose nature is the unfurling of the great vibration (<s>mahānādollāsa</s>) that transcends both struck and unstruck [sound], 'manifests' — the meaning is: it constantly proceeds, through non-instrumental activity, manifesting an emergence in the supreme sky that transcends both conceptual and non-conceptual awareness (<s>savikalpanirvikalpasaṃvid</s>). Thus, amidst the arising of successive masses of phonemes, whose nature is the shining forth of manifold differentiation, between every phoneme from the center, through the sequence of the fourfold speech, with unbroken continuity, without abandoning its own essential nature, according to the method taught face to face — it is the resonance alone that manifests — this is what is stated. // 7 //

children.text:
ādau tāvad vāk-catuṣṭayaṃ nirṇīyate / nirāvaraṇa-niravakāśa-udaya-niruttara-nistaraṅga-parama-nabhasy ucchalat-kimcic-calana-ātmaka-prathama-spanda-vikāsa-svabhāvā varṇa-racanāṃ māyūra-aṇḍa-rasa-nyāyena advaya-mahāsāmarasyataya ānto-dhārayantī para īti prathitā / sa aiva ca anāhata-nāda-svarūpatām avāptā nirvibhāga-dharmiṇī samasta-varṇa-udayaṃ vaṭadhānikāvad anto-dhārayantī draṣṭṛ-svabhāvā paśyanti īti vyapadeśyā / sa aiva ca saṃkalpa-vikalpa-nivaha-niścaya-ātma-buddhi-bhūmiṃ svīkṛtavatī varṇa-puñjaṃ śimbikā-phala-nyāyena anto-dhārayantī madhyama īty-abhihitā / sa aiva hṛt-kaṇṭha-tālv-ādi-sthāna-karaṇa-krameṇā ahatā satī varṇa-vibhava-maya-śloka-ādi-vad bheda-rūpaṃ prakaṭayantī rūpa-ādi-samasta-viśva-prathāṃ ca vyaktatām āpādayantī vaikhari īty uktā / itthaṃ niravakāśāt saṃvit-padāt-
vāk-catuṣṭayam aviratam anirodhatayā prathate / evam īdṛk-svabhāva-vāk-catuṣṭayasya udayaś ca virāmaś ca tāvad udaya-virāmau sṛṣṭisaṃhārau, tayor prathā vyakta-avyaktatayā sada aiva aviratam ullasantyaḥ sphurantyaḥ, tāsu ``svaraḥ'' anāhata-hata-uttīrṇa-mahānāda-ullāsa-vikāsa-svabhāvaḥ ``prathate'' savikalpa-nirvikalpa-saṃvid-uttīrṇa-para-viyad-udayam eva prakāśitaṃ satatam akaraṇa-pravṛttyā prayāti ity arthaḥ / itthaṃ nānā-bheda-ullāsa-prakāśa-rūpeṣu varṇa-nivaha-udvaha-udayeṣu madhyāt prativarṇa-antare vāk-catuṣṭaya-krameṇa akhaṇḍita-vṛttyā sva-svarūpam aparityajya yathā-mukha-upadiṣṭa-nītyā svara eva prathate, --- ity-uktaṃ bhavati //7//

body.text: iti vākcatuṣṭayodayakrameṇa nirāvaraṇasvarodayaḥ sarvatra sarvakālaṃ sphurati, -- iti nirūpya, idānīṃ rasatritayābhoge sati paraṃ dhāmaiva niruttaraṃ cakāsti, -- iti nigadyate
body.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated that the arising of the uncovered resonance (<s>svara</s>) shines forth everywhere at all times through the sequential arising of the fourfold speech, now [the text] states that when there is the enjoyment of the three flavors (<s>rasatraya</s>), the supreme abode itself, unsurpassed, shines forth:

children.text: iti vāk-catuṣṭaya-udaya-krameṇa nirāvaraṇa-svara-udayaḥ sarvatra sarva-kālaṃ sphurati, --- iti nirūpya, idānīṃ rasa-tritaya-ābhoge sati paraṃ dhāma eva niruttaraṃ cakāsti, --- iti nigadyate

body.text: rasatritayāsvādanenānicchocchalitaṃ vigatabandhaṃ paraṃ brahma //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra 8:] Through the savoring of the three essences (<s>rasatritaya</s>), the supreme <s>Brahman</s> wells up desirelessly, free from bondage.

body.text:
rasatrayaṃ gurumukhoditadṛśā manāg īṣat prakāśyate / mūlādhārapayodharādhāraprathitākṛtrimarasatritayābhoge sati "*anicchocchalitam*" niṣkāmatayā prollasitaṃ "*vigatabandhaṃ*" virahitabhedaprathātmakasaṃsārāvagrahaṃ śāntacitrobhayavidhabrahmasvarūpasamuttīrṇaṃ kim api niruttaraprakṛṣṭatarāmarśasaṃvitsvabhāvaṃ "*paraṃ brahma*" eva satatam anastamitasthityā vijṛmbhatety arthaḥ / etad eva rahasyakrameṇocyate / mūlādhāras tu prathamapratibhollāsamahānādaviśeṣaḥ sṛṣṭisvabhāvo bhedābhedātmakasaṃvitpadārthaprathamāśrayabhittimūrtatvāt / payidharas tu payaḥ samastāpyāyakatvāt sarvāśrayasaṃvitsvarūpaṃ tad eva dhārayati sthitipraroham avalambayati yaḥ spando 'dyonmeṣaiva sarvapadārthāvabhāsanāt sthitirūpaḥ / ādhāras tu
jaḍājaḍabhāvapadārthopasaṃhārakatvāt pratyāvṛttisaṃvitsvabhāvaḥ saṃhāraḥ / etattrayodhūtaṃ rasarūpaṃ tattadanubhavacamatkārasāmarasyam āsvādya svātmany akṛtakakhamudrānupraveśād vimṛśya, turyasvabhāvo mahāsaṃhārākhyo 'navarataṃ paramādvayatayā vibhātīti rahasyārthaḥ //8
body.translated_text: The three essences are slightly illuminated by the vision uttered from the <s>guru</s>'s mouth. When there is the enjoyment of the uncreated three essences manifested through the <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root-support), <s>payodhara</s> (nourisher), and <s>ādhāra</s> (support) — 'welling up desirelessly' means shining forth through desirelessness; 'free from bondage' means having transcended the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> whose nature is the manifestation of differentiation, having surpassed the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> of both the peaceful and the variegated kinds — [it is] some indescribable, supremely exalted awareness whose essential nature is the consciousness of the unsurpassed reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), the 'supreme <s>Brahman</s>' itself, which constantly unfolds in an unsetting abiding. This is the meaning. This very [teaching] is expressed through the secret method: the <s>mūlādhāra</s> is the special great <s>nāda</s> (vibration) of the first flash of creative insight (<s>pratibhā</s>), whose nature is creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), because it embodies the foundation-wall that is the first receptacle of the reality of consciousness of the nature of difference-and-non-difference. The <s>payodhara</s> — because it nourishes everything — sustains the consciousness-nature that is the universal support; the <s>spanda</s> (vibration) that supports the growth of stability, that is the very <s>unmeṣa</s> (unfolding) of this [moment], has the form of maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>) because it manifests all realities. The <s>ādhāra</s> is dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), whose nature is the consciousness of turning-back (<s>pratyāvṛtti</s>), because it withdraws the realities of both inert and non-inert states. Having savored the essence-form shaken forth from these three — the equipoise of the wonder of each experience — reflecting upon it within one's own self through the entry into the uncreated <s>khamudrā</s> (sky-seal), that whose nature is the fourth state (<s>turya</s>), called the great dissolution (<s>mahāsaṃhāra</s>), constantly shines in supreme non-duality. This is the secret meaning. ||8||

children.text:
rasa-trayaṃ guru-mukha-udita-dṛśā manāg īṣat prakāśyate / mūlādhāra-payodhara-ādhāra-prathita-akṛtrima-rasa-tritaya-ābhoge sati "*anicchā-ucchalitam*" niṣkāmatayā prollasitaṃ "*vigata-bandhaṃ*" virahita-bheda-prathā-ātmaka-saṃsāra-avagrahaṃ śānta-citra-ubhayavidha-brahma-svarūpa-samuttīrṇaṃ kim api niruttara-prakṛṣṭatara-āmarśa-saṃvit-svabhāvaṃ "*paraṃ brahma*" eva satatam an-astam-ita-sthityā vijṛmbhata ity arthaḥ / etad eva rahasya-krameṇa ucyate / mūlādhāras tu prathama-pratibhā-ullāsa-mahānāda-viśeṣaḥ sṛṣṭisvabhāvo bheda-abheda-ātmaka-saṃvit-padārtha-prathama-āśraya-bhitti-mūrtatvāt / payidharas tu payaḥ samasta-āpyāyakatvāt sarva-āśraya-saṃvit-svarūpaṃ tad eva dhārayati sthiti-praroham avalambayati yaḥ spando 'dya-unmeṣa eva sarva-padārtha-avabhāsanāt sthiti-rūpaḥ / ādhāras tu
jaḍa-ajaḍa-bhāva-padārtha-upasaṃhārakatvāt pratyāvṛtti-saṃvit-svabhāvaḥ saṃhāraḥ / etat-traya-udhūtaṃ rasa-rūpaṃ tat-tad-anubhava-camatkāra-sāmarasyam āsvādya svātmany akṛtaka-kha-mudrā-anupraveśād vimṛśya, turya-svabhāvo mahāsaṃhāra-ākhyo 'navarataṃ parama-advayatayā vibhāti iti rahasya-arthaḥ //8

body.text: evaṃ niravakāśabhaṅgyā rasatritayacarcāsaṃpradāyaṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ devīcatuṣṭayakathāsākṣātkāraḥ prakāśyate
body.translated_text: Having thus established the tradition of the discourse on the three essences through the method without scope, now the direct realization of the discourse on the fourfold Goddess is revealed:

children.text: evaṃ niravakāśa-bhaṅgyā rasa-tritaya-carcā-saṃpradāyaṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ devī-catuṣṭaya-kathā-sākṣātkāraḥ prakāśyate

body.text: devīcatuṣṭayollāsena sadaiva svaviśrāntyacasthitiḥ //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra 9:] Through the shining forth (<s>ullāsa</s>) of the fourfold Goddess (<s>devīcatuṣṭaya</s>), there is constant abiding in one's own repose.

body.text: "*devīcatuṣṭayaṃ*" kṣuttṛḍīrṣyāmananākhyam / tatra ca sarvagrāsaniratatvāt kṣud eva mahāsaṃhāraḥ / sarvaśoṣakatvāt tṛḍ eva saṃhāraḥ / īrṣyā dvayaprathāpādikā grāhyagrāhakaparigrahagrathitā sthitirūpā / mananā ca saṃkalpavikalpollāsarūpā sṛṣṭiḥ / etadrūpasya devīcatuṣṭayasya ca "*ullāsena*" ghasmarasaṃvitpravāhapravṛttyā prathanena "*sadaiva*" sarvakālaṃ pratyekaṃ cāturātmyenodyogābhāsacarvaṇālaṃgrāsavapuṣā svasvarūpāvasthitir pañcamapadātiśāyinī niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā sthitety arthaḥ / /9
body.translated_text: The 'fourfold Goddess' is named hunger (<s>kṣud</s>), thirst (<s>tṛṭ</s>), envy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), and thinking (<s>mananā</s>). Among these: hunger is the great dissolution (<s>mahāsaṃhāra</s>), because it is devoted to devouring everything. Thirst is dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), because it desiccates everything. Envy, which produces the manifestation of duality, woven into the embrace of the grasped and the grasper, has the form of maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>). And thinking, whose form is the shining forth of intention and conceptualization (<s>saṃkalpavikalpa</s>), is creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>). Through the 'shining forth' of this fourfold Goddess of such a nature — that is, through the manifestation and flowing forth of all-devouring consciousness — 'always' means at all times, in each case through the fourfold nature consisting of impulse (<s>udyoga</s>), manifestation (<s>ābhāsa</s>), relishing (<s>carvaṇa</s>), and complete absorption (<s>alaṃgrāsa</s>) — one's abiding in one's own true nature surpassing the fifth state, established in consciousness without scope (<s>niravakāśa</s>). This is the meaning. ||9||

children.text: "*devī-catuṣṭayaṃ*" kṣut-tṛḍ-īrṣyā-mananā-ākhyam / tatra ca sarva-grāsa-niratatvāt kṣud eva mahāsaṃhāraḥ / sarva-śoṣakatvāt tṛḍ eva saṃhāraḥ / īrṣyā dvaya-prathā-āpādikā grāhya-grāhaka-parigraha-grathitā sthiti-rūpā / mananā ca saṃkalpa-vikalpa-ullāsa-rūpā sṛṣṭiḥ / etad-rūpasya devī-catuṣṭayasya ca "*ullāsena*" ghasmara-saṃvit-pravāha-pravṛttyā prathanena "*sada aiva*" sarva-kālaṃ pratyekaṃ cāturātmyena udyoga-ābhāsa-carvaṇa-alaṃgrāsa-vapuṣā sva-svarūpa-avasthitir pañcama-pada-atiśāyinī niravakāśa-saṃvin-niṣṭhā sthita īty arthaḥ / /9

body.text: ity anena sūtreṇa devīcatuṣṭayakathākramaṃ prakāśya, idānīṃ dvādaśavāhacakrarahasyaṃ nirūpyate
body.translated_text: Having revealed by this sūtra the sequential discourse on the fourfold Goddess, now the secret of the twelve-channel wheel (<s>dvādaśavāhacakra</s>) is expounded:

children.text: ity anena sūtreṇa devī-catuṣṭaya-kathā-kramaṃ prakāśya, idānīṃ dvādaśa-vāha-cakra-rahasyaṃ nirūpyate

body.text: dvādaśavāhodayena mahāmarīcivikāsaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra 10:] Through the arising of the twelve channels (<s>dvādaśavāha</s>), the expansion of the great rays (<s>mahāmarīci</s>).

body.text: manaḥsaṃhitaṃ śrotrādibuddhīndriyapañcakaṃ, tathā buddhisaṃhitaṃ vāgādikarmendriyapañcakaṃ, etadubhayasamūhaḥ "*dvādaśavāhaḥ*" / tasyollāso 'hetukena kenāpy ativiśṛṅkhalataradhāmaniruttaranistaraṅgaparasvātantryavṛttyā ghasmarasaṃvitpravāhaḥ / tena "*mahāmarīcīnām*" nirāvaraṇakrameṇa pratyekasmin pravāhodyogāvabhāsacarvaṇālaṃgrāsaviśrāntirūpāṇāṃ mahāsaṃvidraśmīnāṃ "*vikāsaḥ*" niyatāniyatacidacitprathāvigalanena nityavikasvarasvabhāvo mahāprabodhaḥ satatam avinaśvaratayā sarvatra sarvataḥ sarvadaiva sthiteti mahāvākyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The five cognitive faculties (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) — hearing and so forth — conjoined with mind (<s>manas</s>), and likewise the five action faculties (<s>karmendriya</s>) — speech and so forth — conjoined with intellect (<s>buddhi</s>): the aggregate of both these is the 'twelve channels.' Their shining forth is an all-devouring flow of consciousness, operating through an inexplicable, utterly unrestrained, supremely independent, waveless radiance without cause. Through that, 'of the great rays' — that is, of the great rays of consciousness (<s>mahāsaṃvidraśmi</s>), each having the form of repose in the impulse, manifestation, relishing, and complete absorption of flow, [revealed] through the uncovering sequence — the 'expansion' is the great awakening (<s>mahāprabodha</s>), whose nature is eternally unfolding through the dissolution of the manifestation of determined and undetermined, conscious and unconscious — constantly, indestructibly, everywhere, from all sides, at all times it abides. This is the meaning of the great statement (<s>mahāvākya</s>). ||

children.text: manaḥ-saṃhitaṃ śrotra-ādi-buddhīndriya-pañcakaṃ, tathā buddhi-saṃhitaṃ vāg-ādi-karmendriya-pañcakaṃ, etad-ubhaya-samūhaḥ "*dvādaśa-vāhaḥ*" / tasya ullāso 'hetukena kena apy ati-viśṛṅkhalatara-dhāma-niruttara-nistaraṅga-para-svātantrya-vṛttyā ghasmara-saṃvit-pravāhaḥ / tena "*mahā-marīcīnām*" nirāvaraṇa-krameṇa pratyekasmin pravāha udyoga-avabhāsa-carvaṇa-alaṃgrāsa-viśrānti-rūpāṇāṃ mahāsaṃvid-raśmīnāṃ "*vikāsaḥ*" niyata-aniyata-cid-acit-prathā-vigalanena nitya-vikasvara-svabhāvo mahā-prabodhaḥ satatam avinaśvaratayā sarvatra sarvataḥ sarvada aiva sthita iti mahāvākya-arthaḥ //

body.text: ity akaraṇasiddhaṃ sadaiva nirāvaraṇapadasamāveśaṃ dvādaśavāhodayadṛśā prakāśya, idānīṃ caryāpañcakasaṃpradāyaṃ nirūpyanti
body.translated_text: Having thus revealed through the vision of the arising of the twelve channels the absorption into the uncovered state (<s>nirāvaraṇapada</s>) that is always accomplished without [deliberate] action (<s>akaraṇasiddha</s>), they now expound the tradition of the fivefold practice (<s>caryāpañcaka</s>):

children.text: ity akaraṇa-siddhaṃ sada aiva nirāvaraṇa-pada-samāveśaṃ dvādaśa-vāha-udaya-dṛśā prakāśya, idānīṃ caryā-pañcaka-saṃpradāyaṃ nirūpyanti

body.text: caryāpañcakodaye nistaraṅgasamāveśaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Sūtra 11:] Upon the arising of the fivefold practice (<s>caryāpañcaka</s>), waveless absorption (<s>nistaraṅgasamāveśa</s>).

body.text:
"*caryāpañcakaṃ*" tv anāśritāvadhūtonmattasarvabhakṣyamahāvyāpakasvarūpaṃ / tasyodayo niyatāniyataśaktisamūhāntarodito vikāsasvabhāvollāsaḥ / tasmin sati "*nistaraṅgasamāveśaḥ*" āṇavaśāktaśāmbhavodayarūpasamastataraṅgaparivarjitasamāveśalakṣaṇaniruttarasamāveśadharmaiva prathatetyarthaḥ / caryāpañcakakramaṃ ca vitatya nirūpayāmi / tatrānāśritā nirādhāratvāt paramākāśarūpā śrotrasuṣirapradeśagamanena svagrāhyavastūpasaṃharaṇāyodgatā / avadhūtā cāniyatatayā sarvatraviharaṇadṛkśaktimārgeṇa svasaṃhāryasvīkaraṇāyonmiṣitā / unmattā ca vicittavatsvatantratayā grāhyāgrāhyasaṃbandhāvivakṣayā svaviṣayagrahaṇāya prathitā / sarvabhakṣyā bhakṣyasaṃskāranikhilakavalanaśīlā svasaṃhāryapadārthagrasanāyoditā / sarvavyāpikā ca
tvagvṛttigamanikayā nikhilavyāpakatvād aśeṣasparśasvīkaraṇāyonmiṣitā; -- iti caryāpañcakodayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The "fivefold practice" (<s>caryāpañcaka</s>) has the nature of the unsupported, the <s>avadhūtā</s> (the shaken-off), the mad, the all-devouring, and the all-pervading. Its arising is an efflorescence whose nature is expansion, arising within the host of determined and undetermined powers. When that exists, "the absorption without waves" (<s>nistaraṅgasamāveśa</s>) — meaning the very nature of the unsurpassed absorption characterized by absorption free from all waves in the form of the arising of the <s>āṇava</s>, <s>śākta</s>, and <s>śāmbhava</s> levels — manifests. And I shall explain the sequence of the fivefold practice in detail. Among these: the unsupported (<s>anāśritā</s>), being without support, has the form of the supreme sky, arisen for the withdrawal of one's own graspable objects through movement to the region of the aperture of the ear. The <s>avadhūtā</s> (the shaken-off), being unrestricted, has been manifested for the appropriation of what is to be withdrawn by oneself, through the path of the power of vision that wanders everywhere. The mad (<s>unmattā</s>), being independent like one bewildered, having no intention of the relation between graspable and ungraspable, is manifested for the grasping of one's own domain. The all-devouring (<s>sarvabhakṣyā</s>), whose nature is to devour all impressions of what is to be consumed, has arisen for the devouring of the objects to be withdrawn by oneself. And the all-pervading (<s>sarvavyāpikā</s>), through the movement of the activity of touch, being all-pervasive, has been manifested for the appropriation of all touch — thus is the arising of the fivefold practice.

children.text:
"*caryā-pañcakaṃ*" tv anāśrita-avadhūta-unmatta-sarvabhakṣya-mahāvyāpaka-svarūpaṃ / tasya udayo niyata-aniyata-śakti-samūha-antara-udito vikāsa-svabhāva ullāsaḥ / tasmin sati "*nistaraṅga-samāveśaḥ*" āṇava-śākta-śāmbhava-udaya-rūpa-samasta-taraṅga-parivarjita-samāveśa-lakṣaṇa-niruttara-samāveśa-dharma aiva prathata ity-arthaḥ / caryā-pañcaka-kramaṃ ca vitatya nirūpayāmi / tatra anāśritā nirādhāratvāt parama-ākāśa-rūpā śrotra-suṣira-pradeśa-gamanena sva-grāhya-vastu-upasaṃharaṇāya udgatā / avadhūtā ca aniyatatayā sarvatra-viharaṇa-dṛk-śakti-mārgeṇa sva-saṃhārya-svīkaraṇāya unmiṣitā / unmattā ca vicittavat-svatantratayā grāhya-agrāhya-saṃbandha-avivakṣayā sva-viṣaya-grahaṇāya prathitā / sarvabhakṣyā bhakṣya-saṃskāra-nikhila-kavalana-śīlā sva-saṃhārya-padārtha-grasanāya uditā / sarva-vyāpikā ca
tvag-vṛtti-gamanikayā nikhila-vyāpakatvād aśeṣa-sparśa-svīkaraṇāya unmiṣitā; --- iti caryā-pañcaka-udayaḥ //

body.text: satatasiddhacaryākramaṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ nirniketaparajñānaprakāśāvalambanena puṇyapāpanivṛttikathāṃ nirūpayanti
body.translated_text: Having established the method of the practice that is perpetually accomplished, they now expound the discourse on the cessation of merit and demerit by relying on the illumination of the supreme knowledge that is without fixed abode:

children.text: satata-siddha-caryā-kramaṃ nirūpya, idānīṃ nirniketa-para-jñāna-prakāśa-avalambanena puṇya-pāpa-nivṛtti-kathāṃ nirūpayanti

body.text: mahābodhasamāveśāt puṇyapāpasaṃbandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the absorption in the great awakening, there is no connection with merit and demerit.

body.text: "*mahābodhaḥ*" ca jñātṛjñānajñeyavikalpasaṃkalpakāluṣyanirmukto niḥśamaśamāniketanirdhāmadhāmaprathātmakaḥ paratarajñānasvabhāvaḥ kramākramottīrṇatvān mahāgurubhir sākṣātkṛtaḥ / tasya "*samāveśaḥ*" akaraṇakrameṇa yathāsthitasaṃniveśena tyāgasvīkāraparihārataḥ satatam acyutavṛttyā tadrūpeṇa sphuraṇam / tasmāt "*mahābodhasamāveśat*" puṇyapāpayor śubhāśubhalakṣaṇakarmaṇor dvayor svaphaladvayavitaraṇaśīlayor "*asaṃbandhaḥ*" asaṃśleṣo 'saṃyogaś cānavarataṃ jīvata eva vīravarasyāpaścimajanmanaḥ kasya cit sarvakālam akṛtakānubhavarasacarvaṇasaṃtṛptasya bhavabhūmāv eva bandhamokṣobhayottīrṇamahāmuktir karatalāmalakavat sthitety arthaḥ //
body.translated_text: "The great awakening" (<s>mahābodha</s>) is free from the impurity of the conceptual construction of knower, knowledge, and knowable; its nature is the supreme knowledge that transcends sequence and non-sequence, having the form of the manifestation of the abode that is abode-less, of the quiescence that is beyond quiescence and non-quiescence, without fixed dwelling — directly realized by the great <s>gurus</s>. Its "absorption" (<s>samāveśa</s>) is, through a non-instrumental method, in accordance with the arrangement as it stands, by the avoidance of both abandonment and acceptance, a constant unfallen flashing forth in that form. Therefore, from "the absorption in the great awakening," of merit and demerit — the two actions characterized as auspicious and inauspicious, whose nature is to dispense their respective twofold fruits — there is "no connection," no attachment, no conjunction, constantly, for a certain supreme hero who is alive, in his final birth, at all times, satisfied by the savoring of the taste of uncreated experience — the great liberation that transcends both bondage and liberation stands in the very ground of existence like an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit on the palm of the hand — this is the meaning.

children.text: "*mahā-bodhaḥ*" ca jñātṛ-jñāna-jñeya-vikalpa-saṃkalpa-kāluṣya-nirmukto niḥśama-śama-aniketa-nirdhāma-dhāma-prathā-ātmakaḥ paratara-jñāna-svabhāvaḥ krama-akrama-uttīrṇatvān mahā-gurubhir sākṣātkṛtaḥ / tasya "*samāveśaḥ*" akaraṇa-krameṇa yathāsthita-saṃniveśena tyāga-svīkāra-parihārataḥ satatam acyuta-vṛttyā tad-rūpeṇa sphuraṇam / tasmāt "*mahābodha-samāveśat*" puṇya-pāpayor śubha-aśubha-lakṣaṇa-karmaṇor dvayor sva-phala-dvaya-vitaraṇa-śīlayor "*asaṃbandhaḥ*" asaṃśleṣo 'saṃyogaś ca anavarataṃ jīvata eva vīra-varasya apaścima-janmanaḥ kasya cit sarva-kālam akṛtaka-anubhava-rasa-carvaṇa-saṃtṛptasya bhava-bhūmāv eva bandha-mokṣa-ubhaya-uttīrṇa-mahāmuktir kara-tala-āmalaka-vat sthita īty arthaḥ //

body.text: svasvarūpaprāptipūrvakaṃ puṇyapāpatiraskāracarcākramam uktvā, idānīṃ svarasiddhamaunakathām udghāṭayanti
body.translated_text: Having spoken of the discourse on the method of the dismissal of merit and demerit preceded by the attainment of one's own true nature, they now open the discourse on the silence that is accomplished spontaneously:

children.text: sva-svarūpa-prāpti-pūrvakaṃ puṇya-pāpa-tiraskāra-carcā-kramam uktvā, idānīṃ svara-siddha-mauna-kathām udghāṭayanti

body.text: akathanakathābalena mahāvismayamudrāprāptyā khasvaratā //
body.translated_text: By the power of the discourse beyond discourse, through the attainment of the <s>mudrā</s> (seal) of the great wonder, the state of being the resonance of the sky.

body.text:
"*akathanakathābalaṃ*" gurumukhopadiṣṭasaṃpradāyakrameṇa manāg iha carcyate / asya akārasya (1)hata(2)anāhata(3)anāhatahata(4)anāhatahatottīrṇatayā caturdhoditarūpasya kathanaṃ vaktrāmnāyacarcāsaṃniveśanam ity akathanaṃ / tatra hatas tāvat kathyate - hṛtkaṇṭhatālvādisthānakaraṇasaṃniveśair hato 'kārādihakāraparyantanānāpadārthāvabhāsakaḥ / anāhataś cāsvaramūlollasitaparanādavisphāras tantrīmadhyamāsvarasaṃketako 'akaṇṭhakūpāntād upacārataḥ kṛtapratiṣṭhaḥ / anāhatahataś cobhayāśritonmiṣito 'hato viśrāntaśaṣkulīśravaṇagopanodbhinnaprathaḥ śravaṇayugmamadhyavartyākāśāt tattvapratibimbatattvadehato 'pi hato 'nāhatahataḥ / anāhatahatottīrṇaś ca mahānirāvaraṇadhāmasamullasito 'vikalpaḥ
īṣaccalattātmakamahāspandaprathamakoṭirūpaḥ svaraḥ saṃkocavikāsavirahāt paramavikāsarūpo 'sparśadharmānuccāryamahāmantraprathātmakaḥ / tathā cānāhatahatottīrṇo yaḥ sa śṛṅgāṭakākāro raudrīsvabhāvas turyaḥ / anāhatahataś cānackakalātmakavaktrasaṃsthāno vāmarūpaḥ suṣuptaḥ / anāhataś ca bāhurūpāmbikāśaktir yāgame nirūpitā tatsvarūpaḥ svapnaḥ / hataś cāyudhākāro jyeṣṭhāsvabhāvo jāgrat / ity etaccatuṣṭayasvabhāvasyādyavarṇasya kathanaṃ pāramparyamukhayuktiviśeṣaḥ / tasya balaṃ hatādirūpatrayollasitānāhatahatottīrṇarāvasphurattārūpaṃ vīryaṃ tena "*akathanakathābalena*" / tatraivam akathanaṃ vākprapañcottīrṇam akathanam eva kathanaṃ saṃkramaṇakrameṇa nirniketasvarūpāvadhānaṃ tad eva balaṃ akṛtakasphārasāraṃ / tena saṃkramaṇaṃ ca manāg iha vitanyate / prāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyapramātṛniviniṣṭābhimānavigalanena nistaraṅgapravikacacciddhāmabaddhāspado daiśikavaro niḥspandānandasundaraparamaśūnyadṛgbalena kāryakaraṇakarmanirapekṣatayā yad yat kiṃ cit sarvagatātmasvarūpapratipattāv avalokayati tat tat parataracinmayam eva satataṃ bhavati,  iti nāsty atra sandehaḥ / tathā cānyad vyākhyāntaram āha  kathanaṃ tāvat ṣaḍdarśanacaturāmnāyamelāpakramasamūheṣu pūjanakramoditaniyatāniyatadevatācakrāvalambanena sphurati / iha punaḥ pūjyapūjakapūjanasaṃbandhaparihāreṇa śrīmadvātūlanāthādisiddhapravaravaktrāmnāyadṛśā satatasiddhamahāmarīcivikāsaiva sarvottīrṇasvarūpāvibhinnaḥ sarvadaiva sarvatra virājate,  ity akathanakathābalaṃ tena mahāvismayaprāptir bhavatīti saṃbandhaḥ / "*mahāvismayaḥ*" ca vigato vinaṣṭaḥ smayo mitāmitāhaṅkāradarpaḥ sarvollaṅghanavṛttyā svarūpānupraveśaḥ / atha ca mahāvismayaḥ svaparabhedavismaraṇāj jhaṭiti nirantaranirargalakhecaravṛttisamāveśaḥ / saiva sarvamudrāṇāṃ kroḍīkaraṇāt "*mudrā*" tasyā maunapadasamāveśamayatā / tayā hetubhūtayā "*khasvaratā*" trayodaśakathākathanasāmarasyātmakaḥ khasvaras tasya bhāvaḥ sāmarasyaprathanaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ / khasvaras tu kham api bhāvaśūnyam api svena rāti vyāpnoti svīkarotīty ādatte, iti khasvaraḥ //
body.translated_text: "The power of the discourse beyond discourse" (<s>akathanakathābala</s>) — by the method of the tradition taught from the mouth of the <s>guru</s>, [this] is briefly discussed here. The 'discourse' (<s>kathana</s>) of this <s>a</s>-sound (<s>akāra</s>), whose form arises in four ways — as (1) struck (<s>hata</s>), (2) unstruck (<s>anāhata</s>), (3) unstruck-struck (<s>anāhatahata</s>), and (4) transcending the unstruck-struck (<s>anāhatahatottīrṇa</s>) — is the arrangement in the discourse of the oral tradition (<s>vaktrāmnāya</s>); thus 'beyond discourse' (<s>akathana</s>). Among these, the struck (<s>hata</s>) is first described: the struck [sound], produced by the arrangement of the places and organs of articulation — heart, throat, palate, and so forth — manifests the various word-meanings from the letter <s>a</s> to the letter <s>ha</s>. The unstruck (<s>anāhata</s>) is the expansion of the supreme <s>nāda</s> (resonance) that flashes forth from the root of the vowel-less [consonants], having the sign of the middle tone of the string [instrument], with its seat conventionally established from the cavity of the throat. The unstruck-struck (<s>anāhatahata</s>): that which is dependent on both and has opened forth — the unstruck [sound whose] manifestation breaks forth concealed in the repose of the ear-cavity, the struck [sound arising] from the sky situated between the two ears, from the body of the reflection of reality into reality — this is the unstruck-struck. And the one transcending the unstruck-struck (<s>anāhatahatottīrṇa</s>): flashing forth in the realm of the great uncovered [radiance], non-conceptual, having the form of the first point of the great vibration (<s>mahāspanda</s>) whose nature is slight movement, a vowel that is of the nature of supreme expansion due to the absence of contraction and expansion, whose essence is the manifestation of the great <s>mantra</s> that is unutterable and free from the property of contact (<s>asparśa</s>). And thus: that which transcends the unstruck-struck — that has the form of a triangle (<s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s>), is of the nature of <s>Raudrī</s>, and is the fourth state (<s>turya</s>). The unstruck-struck has the configuration of the face (<s>vaktra</s>) whose nature is the <s>anacka</s> vowel, is of the form of <s>Vāmā</s>, and is deep sleep (<s>suṣupta</s>). The unstruck has the form of the arm (<s>bāhu</s>), is the <s>Ambikā</s> power as described in the <s>Āgama</s>, and is dream (<s>svapna</s>). The struck has the form of a weapon (<s>āyudha</s>), is of the nature of <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and is waking (<s>jāgrat</s>). Thus the 'discourse' of this first phoneme whose nature is this fourfold [reality] is the particular method through the reasoning of the lineage transmission. Its 'power' (<s>bala</s>) is the potency whose form is the <s>tā</s>-sound flashing forth from the unstruck-struck-transcendent [state] which is the efflorescence of the three forms beginning with the struck — 'by the power of the discourse beyond discourse.' Therein, thus: the 'beyond discourse' is [that which] transcends the elaboration of speech; 'the discourse that is itself beyond discourse' is the attention to the true nature that is without abode, by the method of transition (<s>saṃkramaṇa</s>); that itself is 'the power' — whose essence is the uncreated expansion. And the transition is briefly unfolded here: through the dissolution of the self-identification that is established in the subjects of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), and the void (<s>śūnya</s>), the excellent teacher, whose seat is bound to the radiance of consciousness that blossoms forth without waves, by the power of the vision of the supreme void that is beautiful in motionless bliss, without dependence on effect, instrument, or action — whatever he beholds in the realization of the true nature of the all-pervading Self, that always becomes nothing but the supreme reality of consciousness. In this there is no doubt. And another interpretation is stated: 'discourse' shines forth in the assemblages of the method of union of the six philosophical systems and the four <s>āmnāyas</s> (sacred traditions), by relying on the circle of determined and undetermined deities that arise in the sequence of worship. Here, however, by abandoning the relation of worshipped, worshipper, and worship, through the vision of the oral tradition of the most excellent <s>siddhas</s> (accomplished ones) beginning with the glorious <s>Vātūlanātha</s>, the perpetually accomplished expansion of the great rays — inseparable from the true nature that transcends everything — always shines everywhere. Thus 'the power of the discourse beyond discourse' — by that, the attainment of the 'great wonder' occurs; this is the connection. And 'the great wonder' (<s>mahāvismaya</s>): [that in which] the pride (<s>smaya</s>) of limited and unlimited ego is gone, destroyed — the entry into one's own true nature through the activity of transcending everything. Or: the great wonder is, through the forgetting of the distinction between self and other, a sudden absorption in the uninterrupted, unobstructed activity of <s>khecarī</s> (sky-moving [awareness]). That itself, because it draws together all <s>mudrās</s> (seals), is 'the <s>mudrā</s>'; its nature is absorption in the state of silence (<s>mauna</s>). Through that [<s>mudrā</s>], which is the cause, 'the state of being the resonance of the sky' (<s>khasvaratā</s>): <s>khasvara</s> is the equalization (<s>sāmarasya</s>) whose nature is the thirteen discourses and the discourse-beyond-discourse; its state (<s>bhāva</s>) is the manifestation of equalization — this is the meaning. And <s>khasvara</s> means: that which pervades (<s>rāti</s>), appropriates, takes hold of even the void (<s>kha</s>) — which is devoid of entities — by its own [power]; thus <s>khasvara</s>.

"*akathana-kathā-balaṃ*" guru-mukha-upadiṣṭa-saṃpradāya-krameṇa manāg iha carcyate / asya akārasya (1)hata-(2)anāhata-(3)anāhata-hata-(4)anāhata-hata-uttīrṇatayā caturdhā-udita-rūpasya kathanaṃ vaktra-āmnāya-carcā-saṃniveśanam ity akathanaṃ / tatra hatas tāvat kathyate -- hṛt-kaṇṭha-tālv-ādi-sthāna-karaṇa-saṃniveśair hato 'kāra-ādi-hakāra-paryanta-nānā-padārtha-avabhāsakaḥ / anāhataś ca asvara-mūla-ullasita-paranāda-visphāras tantrī-madhyamā-svara-saṃketako 'a-kaṇṭha-kūpa-antād upacārataḥ kṛta-pratiṣṭhaḥ / anāhata-hataś ca ubhaya-āśrita-unmiṣito 'hato viśrānta-śaṣkulī-śravaṇa-gopana-udbhinna-prathaḥ śravaṇa-yugma-madhya-varty-ākāśāt tattva-pratibimba-tattva-dehato 'pi hato 'nāhata-hataḥ / anāhata-hata-uttīrṇaś ca mahā-nirāvaraṇa-dhāma-samullasito 'vikalpaḥ
īṣac-calattā-ātmaka-mahā-spanda-prathama-koṭi-rūpaḥ svaraḥ saṃkoca-vikāsa-virahāt parama-vikāsa-rūpo 'sparśa-dharma-anuccārya-mahā-mantra-prathā-ātmakaḥ / tathā ca anāhata-hata-uttīrṇo yaḥ sa śṛṅgāṭaka-ākāro raudrī-svabhāvas turyaḥ / anāhata-hataś ca anacka-kalā-ātmaka-vaktra-saṃsthāno vāma-rūpaḥ suṣuptaḥ / anāhataś ca bāhurūpa-ambikā-śaktir yā āgame nirūpitā tat-svarūpaḥ svapnaḥ / hataś cā ayudha-ākāro jyeṣṭhā-svabhāvo jāgrat / ity etac-catuṣṭaya-svabhāvasyā adya-varṇasya kathanaṃ pāramparya-mukha-yukti-viśeṣaḥ / tasya balaṃ hata-ādi-rūpa-traya-ullasita-anāhata-hata-uttīrṇa-rāva-sphurattā-rūpaṃ vīryaṃ tena "*akathana-kathā-balena*" / tatra evam akathanaṃ vāk-prapañca-uttīrṇam akathanam eva kathanaṃ saṃkramaṇa-krameṇa nirniketa-svarūpa-avadhānaṃ tad eva balaṃ akṛtaka-sphāra-sāraṃ / tena saṃkramaṇaṃ ca manāg iha vitanyate / prāṇa-puryaṣṭaka-śūnya-pramātṛ-niviniṣṭa-abhimāna-vigalanena nistaraṅga-pravikacac-cid-dhāma-baddha-āspado daiśika-varo niḥspanda-ānanda-sundara-parama-śūnya-dṛg-balena kārya-karaṇa-karma-nirapekṣatayā yad yat kiṃ cit sarva-gata-ātma-svarūpa-pratipattāv avalokayati tat tat paratara-cinmayam eva satataṃ bhavati, - iti na asty atra sandehaḥ / tathā ca anyad vyākhyā-antaram āha - kathanaṃ tāvat ṣaḍdarśana-caturāmnāya-melāpa-krama-samūheṣu pūjana-krama-udita-niyata-aniyata-devatā-cakra-avalambanena sphurati / iha punaḥ pūjya-pūjaka-pūjana-saṃbandha-parihāreṇa śrīmad-vātūlanātha-ādi-siddha-pravara-vaktrāmnāya-dṛśā satata-siddha-mahā-marīci-vikāsa eva sarva-uttīrṇa-svarūpa-avibhinnaḥ sarvada aiva sarvatra virājate, - ity akathana-kathā-balaṃ tena mahā-vismaya-prāptir bhavati iti saṃbandhaḥ / "*mahā-vismayaḥ*" ca vigato vinaṣṭaḥ smayo mita-amita-ahaṅkāra-darpaḥ sarva-ullaṅghana-vṛttyā svarūpa-anupraveśaḥ / atha ca mahā-vismayaḥ sva-para-bheda-vismaraṇāj jhaṭiti nirantara-nirargala-khecara-vṛtti-samāveśaḥ / sa aiva sarva-mudrāṇāṃ kroḍīkaraṇāt "*mudrā*" tasyā mauna-pada-samāveśa-mayatā / tayā hetu-bhūtayā "*kha-svaratā*" trayodaśa-kathā-kathana-sāmarasya-ātmakaḥ kha-svaras tasya bhāvaḥ sāmarasya-prathanaṃ bhavati ity arthaḥ / kha-svaras tu kham api bhāva-śūnyam api svena rāti vyāpnoti svīkaroti ity ādatte, iti kha-svaraḥ //

body.text: ṣaḍdarśanacāturāmnāyikasarvamelāpakathātrayodaśakathāsākṣātkāropadeśabhaṅgyānuttarapadādvayatayā kasyacidavadhūtasya pīṭheśvarībhir mahāmelāpasamaye sūtropanibaddho vaktrāmnāyaḥ prakāśitaḥ / tasyaiveha manāk satām avabodhārtham asmābhir vṛttir iyaṃ kṛteti śivaṃ /
body.translated_text: The oral tradition (<s>vaktrāmnāya</s>), [which is] the direct realization of the teaching through the method of the thirteen discourses [that arise from] the discourse of all the unions of the six philosophical systems and the four <s>āmnāyas</s>, [expressed] in the twofold nature of the unsurpassed state (<s>anuttarapada</s>), was revealed to a certain <s>avadhūta</s> (renunciant) by the <s>Pīṭheśvarīs</s> (Goddesses of the Sacred Seats) at the time of the great union (<s>mahāmelāpa</s>), composed in the form of <s>sūtras</s>. This commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on that very [text] has been briefly composed by us for the understanding of the wise. May there be auspiciousness (<s>śiva</s>)!

children.text: ṣaḍdarśana-cāturāmnāyika-sarva-melāpa-kathā-trayodaśa-kathā-sākṣātkāra-upadeśa-bhaṅgyā-anuttara-pada-advayatayā kasya-cid-avadhūtasya pīṭheśvarībhir mahā-melāpa-samaye sūtra-upanibaddho vaktrāmnāyaḥ prakāśitaḥ / tasya eva iha manāk satām avabodha-artham asmābhir vṛttir iyaṃ kṛta īti śivaṃ /

children.translated_text: freed rightly from the delusion of the division between existence and prosperity,
Thus, this supreme secret — the flood of verbal conceptualization — has been spoken.

this incomparable work was made most excellently by someone, from the expansion of consciousness,

samāpto 'yaṃ śrīmadvātūlanāthasūtravṛttiḥ /
kṛtir śrīmadanantaśaktipādānām //
body.translated_text: This glorious commentary on the sūtras of <s>Vātūlanātha</s> is complete. It is the work of the glorious <s>Anantaśaktipāda</s>.

children.translated_text: By the command of the glorious King <s>Pratāpa</s>, for the delight of the virtuous,
this treasure was published by <s>Madhusūdana Kaula</s>.
